cohort: 457 women who delivered a singleton birth at Griffith Base Hospital between July 2018 and June 2019
finding: Labour augmentation and induction were found to be associated with increasing caesarean section rates, both directly through associations with emergency caesarean section and indirectly because previous caesarean section was the most common reason for elective caesarean section.
mod_finding: Augmentation and induction of labor contribute to increasing cesarean section rates: directly via associations with emergency caesarean section, and indirectly because previous cesarean section was the most common reason for elective cesarean section.
